ontology.note: GeoSPARQL geometry, PROV activity and QUDT buffer units. The mode the graph was filtered for is asserted as fw:travelMode on the network entity -- the term reachability already uses for the mode it assumes -- from src/catchments.ts, so it is declared on the release whose definition is that module rather than here. Configuration SHACL is future work.

changes.description: An extract is clipped to the STUDY AREA, not to the box around it. A bounding box is a convenience owed to services that only take one; it is not what a practitioner drew, and on a province-shaped area the difference is a network of two countries -- Ituri's box reaches into Uganda. The practitioner: 'The clip to the polygon study area is what we need as that has been the intent for the study area all along. I have longer workflows because what was intended was not what was implemented -- in the North Kivu health facilities, I needed a clip points to polygon widget for three sources because the study area clip was not implemented.' The ring is indexed by latitude band inside the engine, so testing a province's nodes against a 7,759-vertex outline costs a band lookup each rather than the whole ring: the box still rejects most of a country in two comparisons and the outline decides the rest. Measured 2026-10-22: the same extract gives 122,061 junctions for Ituri's bounding box and 41,425 for a wedge inside it, at comparable time.

evidence.note: Acquisition only; the graph it produces is checked where it is used. The pacing follows the service's own /api/status rather than a client-side guess, measured against OSMnx's behaviour on 2026-10-19.
